parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The Group 2 sulfates and the Group 2 chromates show similar trends in solubility.

Suggest the trend in the solubility of the Group 2 chromates down the group.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Silver(I) chromate, $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$, is sparingly soluble in water.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Write an ionic equation to show the equilibrium between solid $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ and its aqueous solution.

Include state symbols.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The value of the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ is $1.12 \times 10^{-12}$ at $298\text{ K}$.

Calculate the equilibrium concentration of $\text{Ag}^+$, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, in a saturated solution of $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ at $298\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The hydrogenchromate ion, $\text{HCrO}_4^-$, is a weak acid. The $\text{p}K_{\text{a}}$ of $\text{HCrO}_4^-$ is 6.49.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the pH of a $0.0250\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCrO}_4^-$ solution.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{HCrO}_4^-$ can show amphoteric behaviour.

State the formula of:

- the conjugate acid of $\text{HCrO}_4^-$

- the conjugate base of $\text{HCrO}_4^-$

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
Table 2.1 shows some energy changes.

Table 2.1

| energy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| first ionisation energy of silver | +731 |
| second ionisation energy of silver | +2074 |
| first ionisation energy of sulfur | +1000 |
| second ionisation energy of sulfur | +2251 |
| first electron affinity of sulfur | -200 |
| second electron affinity of sulfur | +532 |
| enthalpy change of atomisation of sulfur | +279 |
| enthalpy change of formation of silver(I) sulfide, $\text{Ag}_2\text{S(s)}$ | -33 |
| lattice energy of silver(I) sulfide, $\text{Ag}_2\text{S(s)}$ | -2677 |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Define the term first electron affinity.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the value for the second electron affinity of sulfur is positive.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Construct an equation for the lattice energy of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$.

Include state symbols.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
Calculate the enthalpy change of atomisation, $\Delta H_{\text{at}}$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, of silver using relevant data from Table 2.1.

It may be helpful to draw a labelled Born-Haber cycle.

Show your working.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Suggest how the magnitude for the lattice energy of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S(s)}$ differs from the lattice energy of $\text{Cu}_2\text{S(s)}$.

Explain your answer.
